concept: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure, Chemistry
question: Carbon compounds DO NOT conduct electricity in the molten state because _______.

options.text: bonding in carbon compounds does not involve formation of any ions
bonding in carbon compounds involve formation of ions

solution:
The correct answer is __**bonding in carbon compounds does not involve formation of any ions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Carbon compounds don't have a free electron that is required for electricity transfer thus making them bad conductors.
 
• Carbon compounds consist of molecules in which the atoms are joined by strong covalent bonds. However, the molecules in the compounds are held together by weak forces so these substances have low melting and boiling points.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Due to the strong carbon-carbon single bonds, saturated carbon compounds are often not very reactive.
 
• Alkanes are single-bond C-C saturated carbon compounds.
 
• A general inertness to various chemical reagents is one of the characteristics of alkanes as a class.
 
• Strong connections between C and H can be found.
 
• Unless alkanes are heated to extremely high temperatures, they do not break.
 
• The bonds between carbon and hydrogen are only marginally polarised because carbon and hydrogen have approximately identical electronegativities.
 
• They are hence typically unaffected by the majority of bases.
